name: s3-standard-faults
note: s3-standard (latency, throttling — see that profile) plus fault rates for every write. ASSUMED, not measured: rates many orders of magnitude above real S3 so that a 10-minute chaos run reaches every path. Ambiguous faults (ambiguous = written, then an error; retried = written, then the answer of object_store's own retry) only for objects cairn manages itself (lease, other): on SlateDB's WAL/manifest/SST and on the shared WAL log, AlreadyExists is a fence — a deliberate fence or fail-stop (D12, NW-2), so those only get plain faults. Written 2026-10-14.

put.note: includes conditional PUTs (If-Match / If-None-Match) — no separate figures yet

all.note: copy, rename — cairn barely uses them

slowdown.note: client_retry simulates the 5xx retry loop of the S3 client cairn builds (object_store 0.14: 10 attempts, backoff 100 ms ×2 with jitter, capped at 15 s; 30 s in total — S3_CLIENT_RETRY_TIMEOUT) — exactly what a real node sees

faults.note: every write, every class: 5xx before reaching the store
objects cairn manages itself: written, then an error / written, then the answer of the retry
